metadata.note: The Greenville and Columbia Railroad, connecting South Carolina's capital to the Upstate -- chartered 1845, construction began 1849. Built in stages: Columbia to the Broad River bridge at Alston by Jul 1850 (bridge finished that October), Newberry by Mar 1851, and the full circuitous 160-mile route (with spurs toward Anderson and Abbeville) through to Greenville by 1853. A companion company, the Spartanburg and Union Railroad, completed in 1859, branched off the Greenville and Columbia at Alston and ran via Union to Spartanburg -- giving Columbia two Upstate destinations off the same original trunk. Civil War fighting damaged the railroad's Columbia property, and an 1866 flood destroyed 40 miles of track. Leased to the Richmond and Danville Railroad in 1886, then folded into the Southern Railway in 1894. The Carolina Special (Cincinnati-Asheville-Columbia, 1911-1968) served this corridor in its later decades -- by the early 1960s truncated to a Columbia-Greensboro run -- and was discontinued in 1968, gone before Amtrak began. GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: real-traced through OpenStreetMap active/abandoned-rail data (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search); the Spartanburg branch's real path visibly detours through Union, SC (within 80m of the town center), confirming the 'Spartanburg AND Union' routing. The Columbia-Greenville traced length (110.7 mi) runs notably shorter than the sourced ~147-160 mi historic mileage -- likely reflecting either later track realignment/straightening, or the historic figure including the Anderson/Abbeville spurs not on this direct through route; not fully reconciled here.
